prompt: Explain how doping changes the electrical properties of silicon and how this is used to make a diode.
stmt_text: Explain how doping changes the electrical properties of silicon and how this is used to make a diode.
sol_text:
Model answer:
Pure silicon has few free charge carriers, so it conducts poorly. Doping adds a tiny amount of another element.
Phosphorus (5 valence electrons) gives n-type silicon with extra free electrons; boron (3 valence electrons) gives p-type silicon with holes. Both greatly increase conductivity.
Joining p-type and n-type forms a PN junction with a depletion layer: with forward bias the layer narrows and current flows; with reverse bias it widens and current is blocked, so the diode conducts in one direction only.
